ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a larger black semicircle with AD as its diameter, and the base is labeled from left to right as D, C, B, A; inside this large semicircle, along the three segments DC, CB, BA of the base, three white unshaded semicircles are drawn respectively. The black region is the region inside the large semicircle after removing these three white semicircles. Reasoning: It is known that AB:BC:CD=1:2:3. Let AB=x, then BC=2x, CD=3x, so AD=6x. The area of a semicircle expressed using diameter d is πd^2/8. The area of the large semicircle is π(6x)^2/8; the total area of the three unshaded semicircles is π[x^2+(2x)^2+(3x)^2]/8=π(1+4+9)x^2/8. The shaded area corresponds to 36-14=22 parts, and the unshaded area corresponds to 14 parts, so shaded:unshaded=22:14=11:7.

raw_record.question_text: Four semi-circles are shown with $AB:BC:CD = 1:2:3$. What is the ratio of the shaded area to the unshaded area in the semi circle with diameter $AD$? <image1>

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as one large shaded semicircle with diameter AD, containing three unshaded semicircles whose diameters are the consecutive base segments DC, CB, and BA. From the text, set AB=x, BC=2x, CD=3x, so AD=6x. Use the semicircle area formula A=πd^2/8 for diameter d. The large semicircle has area π(6x)^2/8, and the total unshaded area is π(x^2+(2x)^2+(3x)^2)/8. The shaded area is the large area minus this unshaded sum. Then form shaded:unshaded = [36-(1+4+9)] : (1+4+9) = 22:14 = 11:7.

From the image, the unshaded part consists exactly of the three smaller semicircles on AB, BC, and CD, and the shaded part is the rest of the large semicircle on AD.
